html:
A spiritual movement founded in China in 1992 by Li Hongzhi. It joins slow qigong exercises and meditation with moral teachings built on three words: truthfulness, compassion and forbearance. It draws on Buddhist and Taoist ideas.

It grew fast in the 1990s, when qigong was popular and many Chinese were looking for meaning after the turmoil of the Mao years. Estimates of its followers then run into the tens of millions. In April 1999 about ten thousand practitioners gathered quietly near Zhongnanhai, the leaders' compound in Beijing, to ask for legal recognition.

The Communist Party saw a mass organisation outside its control. In July 1999 the government under Jiang Zemin banned it. Many followers were sent to labour camps and prisons, and human rights groups have documented torture and deaths in custody.

Outside China the movement runs the Epoch Times newspaper and the Shen Yun dance shows, and it campaigns against the party.
